classification.basis: One cross-sectional apparatus schematic with an explicitly radial family of directed straight ion paths. No photographic or natural-object artwork is necessary.

subfigures: A single shared apparatus cross-section, not separate panels.
partsAndCurves: A round upper glass bulb with a narrow lower neck, rounded lower end and an open left sidearm.
The left sidearm opens toward the vacuum-pump label; a separate leftward arrow indicates that connection.
A thin conducting layer follows the inside of the round upper bulb; the source uses a closely spaced inner contour and small coating marks, not a measurement scale.
One narrow metal needle runs up through the lower neck to an unlabeled tip near the center of the bulb. The long stem has schematic hatching.
A leader from the metal-needle label points toward the needle stem below the tip.
A conducting-film leader targets the upper-right inner bulb boundary.
A glass-bulb leader targets the lower-right outer round boundary.
An ion-path label has a small angled/bracket-like leader near the lower-right rays; it is not a particle track or a calibrated angle marker.
pointsRelationshipsAndEndpoints: All illustrated ion trajectories share the needle tip as their radial origin.
Arrowheads point away from the tip and toward the inner conducting-film boundary.
The visible fan extends from the lower-left through the upper semicircle to the lower-right; the lower neck has no added trajectory.
There are no source point names, radius letters, numeric dimensions, scale ticks, degree values, or particle population labels.
scientificLimits: The drawn ray family is an illustration of directions, not a count of helium ions.
No hidden feedthrough, electrical joint, pump component, seal or operating step may be inferred.
The historical voltage, helium pressure, needle polarity and conducting-layer polarity remain in the complete approved text, not invented figure dimensions.
This is the textbook's simplified field-ion projection account, not a calibrated apparatus drawing or construction instruction.

classification.basis: One shared radial projection geometry with named paired points, curved screen and needle-tip profile, directed ion rays, symbolic radii and a common angular sector. The tiny hills are schematic surface texture, not atom silhouettes.

subfigures: One projection construction sharing an unlabeled lower radial origin.
pointsRelationshipsAndEndpoints: A and B are marked on the upper screen arc; A is left of B.
a and b are marked near the corresponding small needle-tip surface interval; a is left of b.
The left radial line passes from the lower common origin through a to A.
The right radial line passes from the same lower origin through b to B, and is nearly vertical in the source.
Both ion arrows point outward from the small surface toward the screen along those rays.
A large-radius indicator labeled R runs from the lower origin toward the left part of the screen, separate from the a-to-A ray.
A small-radius indicator labeled r runs from the lower origin toward the right side of the needle-tip profile, separate from the b-to-B ray.
The same alpha symbol appears twice within the sector between the two projection rays at different distances from the origin.
No numerical radius, numerical angle, scale, calibration or label for the lower origin is given.
partsAndCurves: One broad upper screen arc extends left of A and right of B.
A short curved needle-tip surface with small hill-like corrugations surrounds the a and b locations.
Two small sector arcs mark the alpha angles between the same projection rays.
The helium-ion-path label uses a leader to the nearly vertical ray, not another ion trajectory.
The tungsten-atoms label uses a leader toward the small tip surface, not an isolated atom outline.
scientificLimits: The approved text supplies arc AB = R alpha and arc ab = r alpha with alpha in radians.
The radial projection construction can be regularized exactly, but drawing-space lengths and angle are not measured source values.
The surface hills remain symbolic texture; no atom contour, particle count or literal atom photo is inferred.
The historical radius values and two-million magnification remain source-attributed text, not a scale represented by the drawing.
inspectionPending: One enlarged source inspection will settle the crowded lower radius letter and the two alpha marks before constructing any spec.
